newsitem.title: PhilippineS: Philippine exchange clears creation of conduct body.
newsitem.headline: Philippine exchange clears creation of conduct body.

text.p: The board of the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) has formally approved setting up a business conduct committee, an essential step before the PSE can win self-regulatory organisation (SRO) status, new bourse president Vitaliano Nanagas said on Friday.
The committee will police brokers. It will be composed of five brokers, the chairman of which would be a PSE governor, he said.
The PSE board is also expected to vote on October 23 on a change in bylaws to include two more non-brokers in the 15-man board to have representations from investors and issuers, he said.

SRO status will give the PSE freedom to make and implement its own rules to make member-brokers and issuers more responsible to the investing public. The PSE is currently regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Nanagas also told a news conference he would aim to have of the country's top 1,000 corporations listed in the exchange.
"It is more in the country's best interest that good companies get listed," he said.
To encourage these companies, he said he plans to simplify listing rules.
He added that earlier plans to set up an options and futures board may have to be reviewed.
"We don't know if we have a big enough market," he said.
Though the PSE may not have a problem in financial and index futures, there might not be enough of a market for commodities futures, he said.
